Recorded claim:
An upstream toolkit change removed .plain from global-shared.css, but Thunderbird still used it for several buttons and panels. The 2024 fix defined the class in messenger.css and adjusted the OpenPGP key-details button spacing. In D210267 the author warned that some .plain users might not import messenger.css; reviewer asked for a TODO to remove the temporary utility, and the landed change added it. The current messenger.css still has .plain and the TODO, while current markup and scripts still use the class. A moved shared style must be checked against each document that imports it; a local bridge should state the intended cleanup.

Provenance: c8ed69512530227d71ecd062873fcad4db4e555e17cf6c41e9104db22eeb6d57. Original evidence IDs: b57913974ae7cf214aa61df022a23d028cbb2c71137465db0c67f10a3d5a04eb, b990202c1d234dcea13d9cbc81536d98cd160dfc527cbc9a8ee1409b049c6453, c246b0968f35cf05017d3621dda100f407e7d1ccaab61abeab6f6028685a6874.
This is a recorded historical interpretation, not independent source verification. Source quotes from personal imports or unconfirmed-access records remain private. Historical test results are reported outcomes; no tests were rerun for this backfill.

title: Recorded lesson: When an upstream CSS utility disappears, keep dependent Thunderbird UI working and track its removal
